system.summary: A numbered table of about 1,240 words ([n]^) plus page.row references into a printed English dictionary, with the column marked by one or two bars. The 1078 and 1096 systems share the table but appear to use two different dictionaries (about 780 pp × 29 rows and about 430 pp × 40 rows).
system.sibling_key: 1096 dictionary: unidentified. A spelling dictionary of Entick's kind with 40-line columns, a little less dense than the London Entick of 1788-1800 for A-H and much less dense for R; scanned London Entick editions 1772-1800 and the Murray (New York) editions 1804/1812 are ruled out. 1078 dictionary: unidentified.
system.notes: Two-dictionary split inferred from 233 banked page.row pairs (dict_refs_from_wordbank.tsv).

diacritics.note: One or two bars after the row number mark the dictionary column; a caret marks a table entry.

solution.what: Checked arXiv 2010.04746, github c2huc2hu/wilkinson and this repo; no full reading found.
Extracted 233 page.row→word pairs from the published wordbanks. Page range, row range and alphabetical run split them into two dictionaries.

Tested 16 archive.org scans of Entick's New Spelling Dictionary (1766-1800) against the 198 usable page.row anchors by fitting each anchor word's alphabetical position to a page (alpha_fit.py). Best fits: 1772 (46 within ±1 page), 1787/1788/1791 (42-44); all hits fall in the 1096 chain (p. 133-430).
Tested Johnson abridgements (1786, 1792, 1802 abstract) and a 785-leaf 1805 English dictionary against the 1078 chain.

Read the page images of Entick NSD 1772, 1788, 1795 and 1800 at the 1096 anchor 163.[26]- glorious / 163.[28]- glory. Glorious is on p. 157 (1772) or p. 167 (1788-1800), col. 2, with 38 lines per column; the cipher needs p. 163, col. 1 and up to 40 rows. All scanned Entick editions are ruled out.

Page images at the glory anchor: Entick 1812 has 40-line columns but glory at about p. 150; Webster Compendious 1806 (F at p. 117) and Perry Royal Standard 1806 (J-K at p. 256) ruled out. The 1096 book is bracketed between Entick 1800 and 1812: probably an Entick printing of c. 1801-1811.
Searched for Entick NSD printings of 1801-1811: Google Books has none in full view (1803 Crakelt edition listed, no preview); HathiTrust catalogue blocked by a bot check.

Page images of Entick NSD ed. Lindley Murray, New York 1804 (HathiTrust nyp.33433070243435, pp. 151-164, 262-263): glory p. 151 col. 2 row 3, happy p. 157, home p. 162, receive p. 262-263, against the cipher's 163/171/178/303. The gap grows from 12 to 40 pages, so the 1804 Murray edition and its 1812 reprint are ruled out.

Interpolating decoder (decode.py): alphabetical interpolation between known table and dictionary values, Gutenberg word-trigram beam search. Held-out LoC 3044-3045: 58.6% of 485 tokens, against Chu et al.'s 75.1%.
GPT-2 coordinate-ascent rescoring of the same candidates (rescore.py): 57.9%, no gain; anchors are the bottleneck.
Looked for more anchors: Chu et al.'s Drive scans and spreadsheets deleted (404/410); no online copy of the LoC reproductions of AGI Cuba leg. 2374.

outcome.method_basis: In progress: no scans obtained and no dictionary edition tested yet.
outcome.notes: Neither dictionary identified; Entick London 1772-1800 and Murray 1804/1812, Webster 1806, Perry 1806 and the Johnson abridgements ruled out by page images or fit.
